headline: Markets plunge as Nasdaq falls 5.3%
notes: Global sell-off Friday: Nasdaq -5.3% to 22,079.83, S&P 500 -3.7%, Dow -670 points (-1.4%), VIX jumped 33% to 37; Nasdaq's worst week since 2020.

headline: Houthi missile hits Riyadh tower
notes: Houthi missile struck Riyadh's financial district and damaged the Public Investment Fund tower and other buildings; no injuries reported; Houthis confirmed the strike.
source_name: Sky News / Middle East Eye / The Hindu, via One Turn

headline: Russian strikes hit Kyiv, 8 killed
notes: Overnight Russian missile and drone strikes hit bridges in Kyiv, killing 8 and injuring 28 across nine regions; fresh strikes hit Kyiv again on Friday.
source_name: Just Security Early Edition / One Turn

headline: EU and UK hold Brussels summit
notes: Second EU-UK strategic partnership summit in Brussels; youth mobility scheme agreed (up to 100,000 young people a year both ways), plus food trade and carbon emissions talks.

headline: Anthropic falls 9% on day two
notes: Anthropic (ANT) fell about 9% at Friday's close (down 14% intraday at one point), a day after its Nasdaq debut closed up 17%; investors took profits amid the global tech sell-off.

headline: Cyclone Akvan lands in Odisha
notes: Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur, Odisha, Friday morning (07:30-08:30 IST) with winds 70-80 km/h gusting to 90 km/h; over 300,000 evacuated, no deaths or major damage reported yet.
source_name: Reuters / IMD via The Hindu BusinessLine

headline: COP31 draft drops fossil call
notes: COP31 negotiators in Antalya removed all references to ending fossil-fuel use from the draft deal; Pacific states such as Vanuatu demand a phase-out; talks entered their final day.
source_name: Japan Times / CBC / The Hindu, via One Turn

headline: Fiji, Tonga declare drought emergency
notes: Fiji declared a national disaster and Tonga a state of emergency as El Nino drought reached crisis level; Cook Islands declared an emergency ahead of Cyclone Xavier. Note: declarations reported 20 Nov; Fiji's exact announcement day is 19-20 Nov.
source_name: RFI / RNZ Pacific, via One Turn; International Intrigue briefing

headline: Medvedev beats Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4
notes: Daniil Medvedev beat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4 on Friday night in Turin and reached the ATP Finals semi-finals for the first time since 2023; he faces Alexander Zverev.

headline: Israeli troops cross Gaza line
notes: Israeli forces crossed the ceasefire boundary (Yellow Line) in central Gaza, the first breach since the ceasefire; the army called it a tunnel-demolition operation, Hamas called it a flagrant violation, thousands near Nuseirat fled.
source_name: BBC / UPI / The Hindu, via One Turn

headline: White House fires cyber chief
notes: National cyber director Sean Cairncross was fired after a week of tech outages that hit air travel and email services; Kirsten Davies (Pentagon CIO) will fill the role.
source_name: France 24 / DW / South China Morning Post, via One Turn

headline: Trump pardons Pete Rose
notes: Trump posthumously pardoned baseball star Pete Rose, who pleaded guilty to tax evasion more than 36 years ago and was banned for betting on games; Rose holds the all-time hits record.
source_name: BBC / Japan Times / UPI, via One Turn

headline: Tanker burns after mine strike
notes: A tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran stepped up attacks on tankers; a Pentagon official put the cost of the US-Iran war at $48.3 billion.
source_name: Japan Times / Middle East Eye / CBS, via One Turn

headline: Iraq troops move on Kataib base
notes: Iraqi security forces deployed Friday to Jurf al-Sakhar, a Kataib Hezbollah stronghold, after the PM gave the Iran-backed militia until Friday to leave amid oil-smuggling accusations.
source_name: Euronews / DW / Just Security Early Edition

headline: Russia breaches Polish airspace
notes: Poland's defence minister said Russia violated Polish airspace overnight with three objects (believed to be two missiles and a drone), as Poland prepared joint drills with the Ukraine-supporting Coalition.

headline: Estonia to shut Russia border
notes: Estonia announced it will close its border with Russia for at least six months; a Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman accused Estonia of planning a new Iron Curtain and threatened a response.

headline: General strike over wages
notes: A general strike drew workers and students to nationwide protests in Italy over pay and the cost of living.

headline: Youth strike in 25 countries
notes: A youth coalition called for protests on 20 November in more than 25 countries against the cost of living and militarisation.
source_name: The Straits Times / NZZ, via One Turn

headline: London-born told not British
notes: The UK Home Office told a woman born and raised in London that she is not a British citizen.

headline: Drone strike kills 10 at mine
notes: At least 10 people were killed in a drone strike at the Bajoun mine site, South Kordofan, Sudan; Amnesty International called for an investigation into nine RSF drone attacks on civilians.

headline: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal
notes: A boat carrying 50-100 people sank off Senegal; at least four bodies were found and dozens are missing, while arrivals in the Canary Islands rose by nearly two thirds.
source_name: BBC / Al Jazeera / Euronews, via One Turn

headline: Nearly 600 women killed
notes: Nearly 600 women were murdered in South Africa in three months, according to a report released 20 Nov. Note: single aggregator source; exact figure to be rechecked before use as a number-strip item (used here as a compact title only).

headline: Court reviews Lindela detention
notes: South Africa's High Court examined the detention of asylum seekers at the Lindela centre.

headline: Guinea No. 3 iron-ore exporter
notes: Guinea overtook South Africa and Canada to become the world's third-largest seaborne iron-ore exporter, a major shift in global mineral trade. Note: single aggregator source; compact title only.

headline: Ghana suspends cashew exports
notes: Ghana plans to suspend raw cashew exports for the first three months of each harvest season and levy an export charge to fund domestic processors. Note: single aggregator source; compact title only.

headline: Sudan halts imports from Kenya
notes: Sudan suspended all imports from Kenya in protest after the RSF paramilitary was hosted in Nairobi.

headline: Somalia expels UAE envoy
notes: Somalia expelled the United Arab Emirates ambassador, accusing Abu Dhabi of undermining its sovereignty.

headline: India 159/1 in Wellington
notes: India reached 159/1 at stumps on day two of the first Test in Wellington: Yashasvi Jaiswal 85 and KL Rahul 52 not out, replying to New Zealand's 368 (Henry Nicholls 175 not out, Glenn Phillips 118).

headline: Jepchirchir banned for 3 years
notes: Marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir was banned for three years and stripped of her Sydney Marathon title; Irene Cheptai becomes champion.
source_name: ABC News (Australia) / AllAfrica, via One Turn

headline: Morocco beat Fiji 6-0 at U17s
notes: Morocco beat Fiji 6-0 in the opening Group H match of the U17 World Cup in Doha, while Senegal drew 1-1 with Croatia in Group F.

headline: F1 practice washed out by rain
notes: Opening practice for the Las Vegas Grand Prix was cancelled because of rain with no lap time recorded; Valtteri Bottas returned to the track with Cadillac, which kept him for 2027.

headline: Intuit sells Mailchimp $3.68bn
notes: Intuit announced plans to sell Mailchimp for about $3.68 billion (about a third of what it paid); Intuit shares fell almost 10% even though quarterly profit beat expectations.

headline: Colombia tax protests swell
notes: Unions, students and opposition groups marched in Bogota and other cities against tax reform; they called the first national strike under President Abelardo de la Espriella.
source_name: Al Jazeera / Folha de S.Paulo, via One Turn

headline: Lula backs Sanchez in Spain
notes: Brazilian President Lula appeared in Spain to support PM Pedro Sanchez ahead of Spain's snap election on 29 November.

headline: Brazil recognises Raoni land
notes: President Lula visited Chief Raoni (94) and recognised Kayapo and Yudja ancestral land; researchers also reported the isolated Awa-Guaja group briefly emerging from the forest.
source_name: Al Jazeera / Le Monde, via One Turn

headline: Brazil sells $1bn reserves
notes: Brazil's central bank sold $1 billion of reserves to slow the dollar's rise; the dollar neared 5.93 reais and the real has weakened about 18% in a month.

headline: Tesla opens in Argentina
notes: Tesla opened its first store in Argentina on Friday, expanding its Latin America presence as the country opens its car market.
source_name: Reuters via EIN South America Newswire

headline: Taiex falls 6.2% on Friday
notes: Taiwan's tech-heavy Taiex index fell 6.2% on Friday, taking the full week's loss to 18%.

headline: Indonesia fires may cost $30bn
notes: Economic losses from fires in Indonesia could reach $30 billion, according to research. Note: single aggregator source; compact title only.

headline: Rohingya unwanted in Malaysia
notes: France 24 report on the plight of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia.

headline: Seoul voids ex-PM Han verdict
notes: South Korea's Supreme Court overturned the 15-year prison sentence for former PM Han (linked to President Yoon's 2024 martial-law attempt) and the court ordered a retrial.
source_name: Japan Times / CBC, via One Turn; International Intrigue briefing

headline: India U17 reach Asian Cup
notes: India's U17 team drew 0-0 with Malaysia and finished top of Group E in U17 Asian Cup qualifying, qualifying for the second time in a row.

headline: Kochhar wins golf playoff
notes: Karandeep Kochhar won a two-hole playoff over Gaganjeet Bhullar at the IGPL Pune Invitational, ending Bhullar's three-week winning run.

headline: SBC Medical breach hits 2m
notes: The SBC Medical Group data breach affected more than 2 million people.

headline: GTA 6 sales pass $2.3bn
notes: Grand Theft Auto VI sold more than $2.3 billion according to industry estimates, expected to be the biggest entertainment launch ever. Note: the game launched 19 Nov; the $2.3bn sales figure was first reported 20 Nov.
source_name: BBC Business / BBC Technology, via One Turn
